name: styleforge
description: Per-author Chinese writing-style management for Claude.
long_description: Maintain isolated writing-style libraries for one or more Chinese essay writers. Ingest new corpus with deduplication and snapshots. Get on-demand writing guides via MCP tools and `/style-write` slash commands. Includes feedback intake and rollback for misingested corpus.

data_dir.title: Data directory
data_dir.description: Where styleforge stores authors, corpus, snapshots, and changelog. Pick a stable folder you back up — your corpus lives here.

tools.name: list_authors
tools.description: List all writing-style authors registered in styleforge.

tools.name: create_author
tools.description: Register a new author with a slug and display name.

tools.name: delete_author
tools.description: Permanently delete an author and all their data. Requires explicit confirmation.

tools.name: get_writing_guide
tools.description: Return the complete writing guide for a given author: SKILL_OVERLAY + style-patterns + learned-rules. Call this BEFORE writing in an author's style.

tools.name: sample_corpus
tools.description: Return 1-5 corpus entries from an author, optionally filtered by topic. Bucketed sampling avoids over-representing any single topic.

tools.name: ingest_dryrun
tools.description: Inspect files for ingest without writing. Returns lists of new files, exact duplicates, near-duplicates, and errors. ALWAYS call this before ingest_execute and show the result to the user.

tools.name: ingest_execute
tools.description: Actually ingest files into an author's corpus. Creates a snapshot before writing. Refuses near-duplicates unless allow_near is set.

tools.name: record_pattern_evidence
tools.description: After viewing an ingested article, record its topic tags and which style-patterns it exhibits. This is how an author's style fingerprint accumulates.

tools.name: append_observation
tools.description: Append a candidate-pattern observation to observations.md. Use for novel patterns spotted in a single article that aren't yet in the rule catalog. Stays as observation until cross-corpus stability earns promotion.

tools.name: recompute_stats
tools.description: Recompute pattern frequencies from corpus-index.json. Run after record_pattern_evidence calls.

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Show corpus size, topic breakdown, and pattern frequencies for an author.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Manually create a snapshot of an author's mutable state.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List all snapshots for an author, with timestamps and labels.

tools.name: rollback
tools.description: Restore an author's state from a snapshot. Saves current state as a new snapshot first, so rollback-of-rollback works.

tools.name: record_feedback
tools.description: Append a feedback entry about a recent style-write output.

tools.name: get_feedback_log
tools.description: Read the feedback log for an author.

tools.name: apply_learned_rule
tools.description: After style-feedback skill negotiates a learned rule with the user, persist it to learned-rules.md. Requires user-confirmed rule text.

prompts.name: style-write
prompts.description: Write or rewrite a piece in a specific author's style. Ask for the slug if not provided.
prompts.text:
I want you to write in the style of a specific styleforge author. Follow this protocol exactly:

1. If a slug is given below, use it. Otherwise call `list_authors` and ask the user which one to use.
2. Call `get_writing_guide` for that slug. It returns SKILL_OVERLAY + style-patterns + learned-rules. Read it carefully.
3. Optionally call `sample_corpus` (k=2-3) for grounding examples.
4. Draft the piece. Strict rule: replicate the author's STRUCTURE / SYNTAX / RHETORIC ONLY. Do NOT import the author's political stance into a topic where the user did not ask for it. The user's stated stance always wins.
5. Self-check against the §4 "failure modes" section of style-patterns.md.
6. Deliver. Then ask the user briefly: "Satisfied? If not, tell me what's off and I'll record it via record_feedback so style-feedback can pick it up later."

slug: {{slug}}
task: {{task}}

prompts.name: style-ingest
prompts.description: Ingest new articles into an author's corpus. Always dry-runs first.
prompts.text:
Ingest articles into a styleforge author's corpus. Follow this exactly:

1. Confirm the author exists via `list_authors`. If the slug is missing, ask.
2. Resolve file paths. If the user pasted text rather than file paths, save each piece as a separate .txt file under a sensible name (date + topic stem) before ingesting.
3. **Batch limit: 5 files**. If more, split into batches and walk each batch through the full flow.
4. Call `ingest_dryrun`. Show the user the plan: new_files / exact_duplicates / near_duplicates. If near_duplicates exist, ask the user explicitly: (a) treat as new (allow_near), (b) skip them, or (c) cancel.
5. After confirmation, call `ingest_execute`.
6. **Enrichment step (critical)**: for each new entry, view the source file, then call `record_pattern_evidence` with topics + pattern_ids. Refer to the author's existing style-patterns.md for the pattern_id catalog.
7. Call `recompute_stats`.
8. Report ingested count, snapshot id, and how to rollback if needed.

slug: {{slug}}
files: {{files}}

prompts.name: style-feedback
prompts.description: Digest accumulated user feedback into actionable learned-rules. User confirms each proposal.
prompts.text:
Process accumulated feedback for a styleforge author. Follow this exactly:

1. Call `list_authors` and confirm the slug. If missing, ask.
2. Call `get_feedback_log` to read all undigested entries.
3. Call `create_snapshot` with label `pre-feedback-review`.
4. Group recurring failure modes. Single-occurrence issues are weaker candidates. Contradictory feedback should be SHOWN to the user, not auto-resolved.
5. Present a numbered list of proposed learned-rules. For each: trigger / corrective action / source feedback / confidence.
6. Wait for user accept/reject/edit on each proposal.
7. For each accepted (or user-edited) proposal, call `apply_learned_rule` with the final wording.
8. Briefly report: K accepted, K rejected, snapshot id for rollback.

Never: modify style-patterns.md (that's ingest-review territory), accept proposals without user confirmation, or strip original feedback log entries.

slug: {{slug}}
